CaF2 and SrF2 exhibit unlimited mutual solubility in both the liquid and solid phases.
The azeotropic point in the CaF2-SrF2 phase diagram occurs at a composition of Ca0.582Sr0.418F2 with a minimum melting temperature of 1373°C.
Mixed crystals of Ca1-xSrxF2 were grown in the composition range 0.38 ≤ x ≤ 0.479 by the Czochralski method.
The pulling rate for 18mm diameter Ca1-xSrxF2 crystals was 1.5-2 mm/h.
Homogeneous single crystals of Ca0.582Sr0.418F2 up to 30mm in diameter could be grown by the Czochralski method.
The chemical composition of the crystals and melts was measured using ICP-OES with a precision of around 3% relative standard deviation.
The thermodynamic assessment used non-ideal models for the liquid and solid phases that accounted for independent mixing of the cations and anions.
The thermodynamic assessment agreed with the experimental DTA results within 1K.
The width of the DTA peaks (ΔT = Toffset - Tonset) was 8.1K for pure CaF2 and 9.3K for pure SrF2.
The maximum measured ΔT was 12.3K, observed for compositions of x = 0.5932 and x = 0.1317.
The thermodynamic model for the solid (Ca,Sr)F2 phase used 4 parameters: a = 2046.1957, b1 = -2.3570417, d1 = -0.0045433252, and a31 = -844.93984.
The deviation from ideality was much smaller for the liquid phase compared to the solid phase in the thermodynamic model.
The azeotropic point in the thermodynamic assessment occurred at x(Tmin) ≈ 0.418, slightly different from the experimental value of x = 0.4651.
The measured Sr concentration in the grown crystals matched the starting composition only for the x = 0.40 growth run.
A small positive deviation from the ideality line x_meas = x_0 was attributed to experimental errors in the concentration measurements.
